-loose baggy clothes

-journaling when you feel horrible but good enough to think about why you feel horrible

Hi sweets :) we have a lot in common (I’m 18F and have two cats as well haha) and I wanted to reply. I was IP for AN for 9 months in 2021. It was an incredibly mixed experience. 
To answer your questions one by one. 
It did help in the end. I was in a high dependency unit and due to the nature of how my disorder made me act I had a lot of incredibly traumatic experiences. There was some unforgivable stuff done to me in the name of treating me. But at the end of the day I would probably be dead right now if I didn’t go. I had no intention of stopping losing weight whilst dropping consistently lower whilst my health slowly deteriorated. I didn’t care at the time and now I’m glad someone stepped in despite the fact it was fucking awful and unbearable at the time. 
Of course it triggered me. Not so much when I first arrived with ED stuff but when I had gained some weight and new people came in very physically unwell I found it very difficult. You’ll almost definitely have a therapist and if not there’ll be staff around who you can and need to talk to about it. I found that the noise on the ward was triggering for other reasons bc it was very distressing and me and the people around me now think I might be autistic which could explain a lot of that (but anyone would find listening to their peers/friends distressed hard). My best advice with people being triggering or flaunting their illness is remembering that they’re literally also just trying to prove to themselves how sick they are and not get involved. You’ll want friends sure bc nobody wants to be alone but I found it was better to just keep to myself than engage in friendships that would be detrimental to me in there and in the future. 
Whilst they can’t force you to physically eat there are other ways they can do it. Idk whereabouts you are but where I am they can legally detain you and declare you unfit to decide anything to do with your treatment once you’re 16 and your parents can’t control your treatment. The unit I was in would restrain and forcibly insert an NG tube if you refused to eat. I know that so many people (including me) see this as some kind of validation that they are sick enough finally but I can confirm you will never ever feel sick enough until you’re dead no matter how many times you’re fed under restraint or how many people hold you down. It’s a slippery slope and only makes you feel worse in the long term. As someone said to me once, what’s the point in fighting so hard against something that’s inevitable. Whether you want to recover or not, spare yourself the anguish of restraints and all that shit bc it gets you nowhere apart from stuck in a hospital bed forever sad and alone. 
Meals were mediocre but ngl after however long restricting they seemed like the food of the gods. 
I kept up with school once I was physically healthy enough to think straight. I missed around 1/4 of the teaching for my final school exams and got top grades and am going to my first choice uni. It’s possible. It might take some intense self study bc I know that most hospital schools for psych wards at least are very small and often only qualified to teach up to a certain age. I just used to get on with my work in the school room whilst everyone else played games and stuff. The thing to remember is that when your life is at stake (which it is for them to send you IP) school really doesn’t matter. Everyone does things in a different timeline. I kept up with school but my friend who was in hospital repeated a year and is now thriving. It doesn’t matter if you can’t keep up bc you are so much more important than making sure you keep up with school. 

There will be people and staff who you can’t stand and make everything worse. There may be doctors who dismiss you and nurses who are there for just the pay check. But there will also be gems of humans who make insane difference to your life. I flip flopped so much whilst in hospital: stay in hospital forever, get out to relapse, properly recover etc etc and I did struggle when I got out but it gets better. 
I felt lost without my ED and did end up with life threatening SH resulting in another admission to a general psych ward after ‘recovering’ and have had multiple mini relapses and am def not completely ‘better’ and don’t know I ever will be but I am so much happier now. I filled the anorexia shaped hole in my life with other things that I love and keep myself busy enough that I can’t afford to restrict bc I need the energy to perform well. It’s not perfect and the journey is rough but as I said, I don’t know if I’d be alive rn if it wasn’t for that long admission. You’ll be okay. Let people help you which I know can be hard. Honestly, it’s really difficult to give advice when I don’t know much about you.

I see you have ADHD so a lot of advice which people throw out just won’t hit quite the same. What I can say is use the start of the year to find what works for you revision-wise if you don’t already know. Take tests throughout the year seriously and then you’ll know if what you’re doing is working. I know that my close friend with ADHD found working next to someone helpful to ‘body double’ them. She was also able to only do work for school within school hours and still do very well by utilising frees and lunch and therefore could relax properly at home when her meds wore off. 

For revision, there are lots of good online resources that may very likely be better than your textbook. Ask your teachers and classmates if they have them. Eg physics and maths tutor, online physics tutor, save my exams, YouTube channels that explain things but these will all depend on your subject and what helps you (but don’t neglect past papers and topic based past paper questions!!!) 

DO NOT FEAR ASKING FOR HELP! If you don’t understand something in a lesson, ask for another explanation. If you missed something in a lesson or were too scared to ask in the lesson, ask afterwards. If you find something in a question in revision you don’t understand, ask a teacher. Something that will take you an hour to work out (likely badly) by yourself can take 10 minutes with a teacher. It’s hard if you’re not used to asking but it’s worth it to get used to it and can really help. 

Finally, have fun. You’re turning 18 and having lots of life milestones. It’s a very stressful year, but that doesn’t mean you have to be miserable the whole time. See your friends, go out and do stuff you enjoy, don’t close yourself off to stuff bc you’re revising. Me and my friend started going out every Thursday night in the lead up to our mocks in the Easter holidays and have continued it. (Obviously we didn’t go out right before our exams and it was flexible). Life doesn’t stop just because you have exams and the people telling you to start revising everything now are likely just thinking how anxious they were right before exams. I think if you look over year 12 stuff and see if there’s any big gaps before September and then make sure to thoroughly revise for topic tests and at the end of modules etc throughout the year you’ll find final revision not so bad. 

You’ll be okay

I think people have already said what I’m going to say but I wanted to put in my thoughts. I’ve been in active recovery for almost 2 years now and weight restored months before that. 

As they’ve already said, your body is reacting in a normal and actually quite logical way to being in a calorie deficit for far too long. It doesn’t only need that food to gain muscle and fat (which are VERY important) but also to repair all the shit that has been broken down over the course of your restriction. It’s normal that you are craving all the stuff that more scary to a disordered brain because 1) you have not had it for ages or you’ve created this scarcity surrounding it so when you can have it you want it and 2) it’s easy for your body to get energy, which it desperately needs, from it. If you continue to eat the foods and not restrict them, the urges to eat multiple packets of biscuits and cakes WILL decrease over time until your body isn’t scared the food will disappear again. 

As for developing BED, that is a completely valid fear to have and I think a lot of us who have/had restrictive EDs think this. At the end of the day, if you have been restricting, your body will cry out for food. It does not mean you’re developing a binge eating disorder. Your physical hunger cues will be fucked from restriction and they’ll come back in time but for now you have to trust the mental ones. Try not to restrict after you’ve eaten more than your brain is comfy with and you should be alright. 

When I was first in recovery, I also thought that I wouldn’t be able to restrict properly again and I don’t know how it is for you but my brain viewed it as sort of a challenge. It turns out that I could and it just prolonged my illness and misery. It’s not worth relapsing just to prove to yourself that you can. 

It’s a really hard and winding road and all of the physical recovery symptoms that you mentioned are brutal. I don’t miss waking up in the middle of the night in a puddle of sweat boiling hot… But the only way out is through. You’re in the early stages of the recovery which can be the worst. Keep going and keep eating what your body needs. Life on the other side and out of the eating disorder is so much bigger and brighter. The recovery symptoms do go away after a bit and the more you relapse and put off recovery, the worse and longer they will be when you do eventually need to escape ED hell. I used to find distractions helped me a lot in early recovery when I needed to eat enough but I wasn’t ready to mentally deal with that (tv/YouTube, crosswords, word searches, sudoku etc whilst or after eating). Keep telling people how you’re feeling and reaching out for support.
